title: docs(plugin-detail): state the Reference Rail opt-in and the option its count is read from
body:
Fixes #7998

`packages/plugin-detail`'s "Reference Rail decision matrix" carried two prose claims the shipped synth does not honour. Documentation only — the synth is untouched and nothing moves at runtime.

## Claim 1 — "emits automatically when:"

The rail is an explicit opt-in. The first conjunct of the shipped condition is `options.showReferenceRail === true`, and the page never mentioned that flag at all, so it described a default that does not exist: a caller who satisfies every listed condition and does not pass `showReferenceRail` gets no rail. The lead-in now says the rail is off by default and that the synth emits it only when the `buildDefaultPageSchema` call opts in with `showReferenceRail: true`.

## Claim 2 — rung 2 pointed at the wrong source

Triage called this the more expensive of the two, because a reader debugging a missing rail goes and inspects field metadata when the answer is in the `buildDefaultPageSchema` call. The code reads `options.related` — the synth CALLER's option — while the page said the objectDef declares them. Rung 2 now reads:

> That same synth call passes **≥2 entries** in its `related` option — the count is read off the caller's option, **not** off the objectDef.

The corrected prose also quotes the shipped conjunction verbatim — `options.showReferenceRail === true`, `!options.hideReferenceRail`, `Array.isArray(options.related)`, `options.related.length >= 2` — so the next drift shows up as a diff against this page rather than as silent rot.

## What this PR deliberately does NOT do

- **The synth is unchanged.** The code is right and the document was wrong.
- **Rungs 3 and 4 are untouched, byte for byte** — both appear as unchanged context lines in the diff. Rung 3 (viewport ≥ xl) reads correct: it is the `hidden xl:flex` class the synth puts on the `aside` region, not part of the `willEmitRail` expression, and the new paragraph says so. Rung 4 had already been repaired under objectui#5174 batch 17.
- **The retired `objectDef.detail.*` route is not resurrected** — this package's CHANGELOG records it as an ADR-0085 removed dead read.

## The pin — what it holds, and what it cannot

Documentation-only, so the honest answer is split in two.

**What is now pinned.** The new `### Opting in` block is a fenced `ts` snippet in a document `check:doc-snippets` covers, so it is compiled `--strict` against the package's BUILT `dist/index.d.ts` on every run of that gate. That holds the load-bearing half of both claims: `showReferenceRail` and `related` are `BuildPageOptions` keys — options of the `buildDefaultPageSchema` call — and not objectDef keys.

Reverse verification, run from the committed fix: renaming the snippet's `showReferenceRail` to `showReferenceRailX` (mutation proven on disk by blob hash, then restored, `git diff HEAD` empty) turns the gate RED. The gate printed, as its own computed diagnostic:

```text
TS2561: Object literal may only specify known properties, but
'showReferenceRailX' does not exist in type 'BuildPageOptions'.
Did you mean to write 'showReferenceRail'?
```

Semantic phase under the mutation: 672 of 672 blocks judged, **1 failed**. Restored, the same gate reports 672 of 672 judged, **0 failed**.

**What is NOT pinned, and nothing here pretends otherwise.** No gate in this repository reads PROSE. The threshold value (≥2), the strictness of `=== true`, the word "automatically", and rung 3's viewport are prose, and the snippet cannot hold them — a snippet passing a single `related` entry would still compile. That is why the shipped conjunction is quoted verbatim instead of paraphrased: it is the cheapest thing a future diff can catch. No test was invented that asserts a string this PR also wrote.

## Verification

| run | verdict |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec turbo run build $(node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter) --concurrency=2` | 35 successful, 35 total |
| `node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` | exit 0 — 672 of 672 blocks judged, 0 failed |
| ablation + restore (above) | exit 1 with TS2561 on this README; restored, blob hash back to HEAD |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/relatedListParentScopeResidue-8937.test.ts` | 1 file, 8 tests passed |
| `pnpm check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-types`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:readme-exports`, `pnpm docs:check-links` | all exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — "no changeset is owed" |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test packages/plugin-detail/README.md` | exit 0 — NOT GOVERNED |

Heavy runs went through the shared serialisation lock in `../objectstack`; the longest hold was 97s.

**Test scope, declared.** The test this repository's own ledger names as the reader of this file is the single one in the table: `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --changed packages/plugin-detail/README.md` returns that path, and `--list` maps it to exactly that test file. No package source changed, so no other unit test can observe this diff. `eslint` does not lint this file at all — `pnpm exec eslint packages/plugin-detail/README.md --format json` reports it "ignored because no matching configuration was supplied" (1 file, 0 errors, 0 lintable), so a markdown-only diff cannot move any TypeScript file's lint verdict. The repo-wide runs remain CI's.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope finding, reported and deliberately NOT patched here: **the live option's own docblock still teaches the retired route.** `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` carries, on the `showReferenceRail` declaration itself, the parenthetical "per object via `detail.showReferenceRail`" — a third instance of the objectDef `detail.*` route that ADR-0085 removed, sitting outside this card's two prose claims. With a firing positive control, `git grep` over `packages/` finds no source read of any `detail.*` rail key; the only non-CHANGELOG hit is that docblock. It travels in the structured report for the triage seat to file. This PR does not touch the synth.
